note: Curated vibe-coding tips. These are editorial guidance (status: interpretation), not claims that code was executed. Illustrative diffs are labelled as such on screen.

tips.title: Stop your coding agent from breaking your UI
tips.hook: Your coding agent keeps breaking your UI?
better: Keep its props and tests unchanged.
Use existing design tokens, no new colors.
tips.notes: Vague requests like make the dashboard look better let a coding agent change any file and any style. Naming the one file to edit, the props and tests to keep, the design tokens to use, and asking for the diff before applying limits the scope of the change and gives you a check before anything lands.

tips.title: Debug with AI without random rewrites
tips.problem: rewrites half your code to fix one bug
better: Here is the failing test and the error.
tips.notes: Fix this bug gives the agent no evidence, so it guesses and may rewrite unrelated code. Giving it the failing test and the error, asking for the root cause first, then the smallest fix, and forbidding changes to unrelated files keeps the fix small and reviewable.

tips.title: Make your agent plan before it codes
tips.hook: Never let your agent start coding first.
better: First write a plan: files and steps.
Run the tests after each step.
tips.notes: Asking an agent to build a whole app in one go means mistakes surface late. Asking it to first write a plan with the files and steps, wait for approval, implement one step at a time and run the tests after each step lets you correct the direction early.

tips.title: Use a failing test as the spec
tips.hook: Give your agent a test, not a wish.
tips.problem: says it works when it doesn't
better: Write a failing test for empty emails.
Run it and show it fails.
Make it pass without editing the test.
tips.notes: Add input validation is open ended. Asking for a failing test first, showing that it fails, then making it pass without editing the test turns the request into a clear definition of done that the agent cannot quietly change.
